description: The New Zealand Geotechnical Database is an online database that consolidates new and existing geotechnical information into a searchable platform. According to the Tonkin + Taylor project page, the firm's engineers and IT developers designed it with the Canterbury Earthquake Recovery Authority, the Department of Building and Housing (now MBIE) and the Earthquake Commission, which contributed about 30 million dollars of commissioned data. It builds on the Canterbury Geotechnical Database, developed to support the Christchurch rebuild after the 2010 and 2011 Canterbury earthquakes, and incorporates the former Auckland Geotechnical Database set up by Watercare. The database is open to professional engineering firms, local and central government, scientific and academic institutions, the Earthquake Commission and insurers, and it has been running since 2012 with MBIE as the client, with GIS integration and an API. Access is by registration for the eligible user groups; no licence or cost is stated on the page read, which is the builder's project page. Caveats: the facts come from the developer's page, not the database itself, and access rules may differ by user type. Coverage is New Zealand. It supports liquefaction and ground condition analysis for pipes, roads, bridges and buildings, such as calibrating fragility of buried networks in earthquakes; related records are the New Zealand Natural Hazards Portal and the Christchurch 2011 earthquake lifelines case study.
